name: Alexander
overview: Alexander is a male figure identified in Scripture as the son of Simon the Cyrene. His mention is brief and specific, with no further tribal affiliation or detailed notes provided. His unique attribute distinguishes him primarily by his paternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Alexander appears in the biblical text without an accompanying meaning or divine attribution. It is presented simply as a proper name without additional significance noted.
familyAndRelationships: Alexander is identified as the son of Simon, who is called the Cyrene, indicating a familial relationship explicitly recorded in Scripture. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Alexander's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his identification as the son of Simon the Cyrene, who is known for carrying the cross of Jesus. This connection situates Alexander within the context of the Passion narrative, highlighting the familial link to a key figure involved in Christ's crucifixion journey.
